reporting-org.narrative: Siasa Place (SP) is a civic-tech youth-led non-governmental organization (NGO), established in 2015 that specializes in working with grassroots youth, in building institutional structures to support youth participation in politics and good governance. SP targets youth (men and women aged 18 to 35 years) and develops their skills in policy review, supporting the creation of youth-friendly platforms for public participation in decision-making processes, including the budget process and social accountability. SP works in 12 counties including Uasin Gishu, Kakamega, Busia, Kisumu, Homa Bay, Migori, Kericho, Nakuru, Nairobi, Kitui, Lamu, and Mombasa.

title.narrative: Strengthening the Power of Youth Voices Quarterly Progress Report: April 2025 - June 2025

description.narrative: The program implemented a wide array of interventions to enhance youth engagement in civic and governance processes, including 7 party branch building activities, 2 gumzo mtaani activities, 2 intergenerational activities were conducted across the five counties, 8 community Sports Dialogue Forums in in Busia, Homa Bay, Kericho, Kitui, Lamu and Nairobi; Additional activities included ongoing social media engagements, social media campaigns, social media leadership accountability board, collectively, these interventions reached 100,851 participants. Out of which 1914 offline (1155 men, 759 women, and 69 persons with disabilities) and 97,986 online (85,645 reached and 12,341engaged) and involved 33 government officials from both national and county levels, including area chiefs, ward and village administrators, members of county assemblies, youth officers, gender officers and registrar of persons. The forums created a platform for public awareness on the rights, feedback on civic and governance challenges affecting the youth and developing advocacy strategies to address the concerns. For the period, 45 civic and governance challenges affecting young people were identified and 15 addressed including Reopening of Kericho Forest Dispensary and Tarmacing of Mail 4 road in Chepseon ward, Kericho County, Completion of Kanziko Stadium Pavillion, Installation of security lights at Kanziko Stadium, reinstallation of electricity transformer at Ekani Village in Kanziko, Kitui County, Repair of Community Water point in Bukhori village – Bunyala North, and murraming of Munana -Sigalame - Sioport Road, Samia sub-county, Busia County, construction of a new mortuary at Mbita Sub county hospital, installation of a new transformer at Kisui and Kirambo village, completion of Thuon Gweno Health centre with new toilets, Maintenance of Nyalkinyi – Otaro road, construction of Nduta bridge in Central ward in Homabay county. Completion of Mlachake – Lake Kenyatta Primary school road, in Bahari ward, Lamu County. These completed projects impacted the community's lives positively. Implementation of agreed advocacy follow-ups and the use of social media for advocacy among county-based youth platforms have greatly improved, out of the 15 completed projects, 8 were advocated for through social media. Follow-up efforts are gaining track, and most online accountability initiatives at the county level are now led by organized groups as opposed to previously being led by individual champions. In response, the program is providing consistent support to group leadership while working with both individual champions and youth groups to build collective capacity. To enhance sustainability, the program is also establishing a collaborative platform that brings together individual advocates and group administrators to facilitate knowledge sharing and joint learning ultimately strengthening group-based advocacy and fostering more resilient accountability structures.
